parent.virtue: Courage, and helping someone who is scared
science: The station goes all the way around the Earth in about an hour and a half, so astronauts see about sixteen sunrises every day.
On the night side, the station is in Earth's shadow; city lights glow on the Earth below.
Fans hum all day and night, because in space air doesn't move around by itself.
The water machine cleans water so it can be used again and again.
Night in orbit is short: the Sun comes back in about half an hour.
parent.summary: The station sails into Earth's shadow and starts making noises. Button is scared. The crew helps Button find out what each noise is.

options: Behind the big blue bag, or under the table: either way, it's a floating spoon.

paths.moment: Go look together, or hide under the blanket
options: Together: hand in hand, they float to the dark tunnel.
Blanket: it's dark and stuffy, and the gurgle doesn't stop. Button bravely peeks out and suggests going together.

talk: What helped Button feel less scared?
What can you do when a friend is scared?
How many sunrises do astronauts see in one day?

beats.say: Star Station zooms around the Earth so fast, it goes all the way around in about an hour and a half.
That means a sunrise, and a sunset, again and again. Astronauts see about sixteen sunrises every single day!
And right now, the Sun was setting.
{T}, can you help the sunset? Tap, tap, tap, and watch the colors change!
The station sailed into Earth's shadow, on the night side of the world.
Inside, the lights turned soft and dim. Nighttime lights.
And then, the station started to make noises.
Hmmmmmmmm.
Clink. Clink.
Gurgle, gurgle, gurgle.
"B-b-beep," said Button. "What was that?"
Button zipped behind {crew}, and peeked out, all wobbly.
Button was scared.

choice.say: {A}, Button is scared. How can we help?

beats.say: [{a} held one of Button's hands, and {t} held the other.|{a} held Button's hand, nice and tight.]
"[We're|I'm] right here," said {a}. "Let's find out what the noises are. Together."
Click! {a} switched on the flashlight. A warm circle of light glowed on the wall.
"There," said {a}. "Now we can see. Let's find out what the noises are. Together."
Button stopped wobbling. Just a little.
Hmmmmmmmm. The first noise was coming from a little grille in the wall.
"Oh! That's a fan," said Button. "In space, air doesn't swirl around by itself, like it does on Earth. So fans keep the fresh air blowing, all day and all night."
{T}, can you feel the breeze? Tap anywhere, and make it swirl!
Button giggled. "The fan tickles!"
Clink. Clink. Clink.
"Where is that coming from?" whispered Button.
{crew} peeked behind the big blue bag.
Clink. Clink. And there it was! A floating spoon, bumping softly against the wall.
{T}, can you make the spoon go clink? Tap anywhere!
{crew} peeked under the table.
Clink. Clink. And there it was! A floating spoon, tapping against a table leg.
{T}, can you make the spoon go clink? Tap anywhere!
"Somebody forgot to Velcro the spoon!" said Button.
{T}, can you stick the spoon back on the Velcro? Tap the spoon!
Rrrip... stick! No more clinking.
Two noises found. One more to go.
Gurgle, gurgle, gurgle. It came from the dark tunnel at the end of the station.
Button's antenna wobbled.
{crew} and Button dove under a big, floaty blanket.
It was very dark under there. And a little bit stuffy.
Gurgle, gurgle, gurgle, went the noise. Hiding didn't make it stop.
"I still don't know what it is," said Button, in a tiny voice.
Then Button did something brave. Button peeked out from under the blanket.
"If we go together," said Button, "I think I can do it."
"Let's go together," said {a}.
Button took a big breath. Well, robots don't really breathe. But it was a big breath, anyway.
Hand in hand, they floated into the dark tunnel.
Gurgle, gurgle... GURGLE!
And there it was. A big white box, with little green lights, blinking.
"It's the water machine!" said Button. "It cleans our water, so we can use it again and again."
"Gurgle," said the water machine, very politely.
Button laughed. "I was scared of a water machine!"
{T}, can you say hello to the water machine? Tap anywhere!
Back at the big window, the Earth was dark. But not all dark.
Down below, tiny lights glowed, gold and white. "Cities," whispered Button. "Where people are sleeping."
Night on the station doesn't last long. Soon, in less than an hour, the Sun comes back.
{T}, can you help the Sun come up? Tap, tap, tap!
A thin line of orange light glowed along the edge of the Earth. Then gold. Then bright, bright blue.
Sunrise!
"I was scared," said Button. "But you stayed with me. And now I know all the noises."
Hmmmmmm, hummed the fans. Gurgle, said the water machine.
And this time, Button hummed right along.
